newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIJATOVIC DEDICATES GOAL TO SICK SON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIJATOVIC DEDICATES GOAL TO SICK SON.

text.p: - Pedrag Mijatovic did not know whether to laugh or cry when he scored Real Madrid's spectacular second goal in their momentous victory over Barcelona on Saturday night.
As he celebrated, arms outstretched in acclaim to the huge crowd in the seething Santiago Bernabeu stadium, the Montenegrin striker thought of his team mates, his high ambitions and the roaring fans.
But above all he remembered his two-year-old son Andrea, lying in hospital recovering from brain surgery, after suffering from birth with excess fluid on the brain.
His plight united supporters and players in sympathy on Saturday and the crowd sang the boy's name.
"He has been ill since he was born but he is out of danger now," said Mijatovic, who dedicated his goal to his son.
"The goal and the result, against Barcelona, made me so happy -- these players here are the best team mates I could have in the world. They were wonderful in their actions for me.

"(Fernando) Hierro (the Real Madrid captain) gave me his shirt for my son, the fans chanted his name and I felt myself wanting to cry. I will never forget this match. It has been a very significant one for us all."

Madrid's other goalscorer, the Croatian striker Davor Suker, dedicated his 13th goal of the season to little Andrea in a gesture which showed the two Balkans are as much in tandem off the pitch as on it.
"We were all thinking of Andrea and it was my only thought," said Suker. "Pedja is a good friend for me and a great player."

The co-operation between the two exemplified the Spanish first division's to unify Croatians, Bosnians, Serbs and Montenegrins on one sporting stage as well as highlighting the arrival of the skilful man from Podgorica.
"The war was a long and painful process," Mijatovic, who joined Madrid this year after scoring 28 goals in his third season with Valencia, told the Real club's monthly magazine.

"But I had a lot of luck not to lose any friends or relatives in the armed conflict -- all that happened away from Montenegro in Croatia or in Bosnia. Now I have no problem playing with players from these other places in our league, none at all.
"It is obvious from my relationship with Davor, for example. He is a Croat and we are great friends. We have never allowed the conflict to interfere in our lives here."
Born in Podgorica, Mijatovic, who turns 28 next month, rose to prominence with Partizan Belgrade before joining Valencia in 1993.
"Where I grew up everyone wanted to play for Real Madrid," he said. "They have always been the most famous team in the world for us.
"When I had the opportunity to come to Spain and play for Valencia, I was delighted to have the chance to prove myself because I hoped it might give me a chance to play for Real Madrid.

"In my childhood, that was the dream. But now my ambitions are bigger. After three years at Valencia, where I was very happy and the people were wonderful, I want to do more and win three titles with Real. I want to play in the Champions League and to win it at least twice and I want to be the best player in Europe.
"I know these sound like big ambitions, but they are what I am aiming for and I am hoping and working to be successful."

Father-of-two Mijatovic was regarded as the finest player in Spain last season with Valencia, before transferring to the capital, and says that being lauded as the finest Montenegro player is an honour.
"I am very ambitious and very serious about my football and I want to reach the very top. That is why I am here in Spain, with Madrid, and why I feel so much emotion in my game.
"Playing here is the biggest thing in my life -- after my family, of course -- and I am very happy to be here."
This weekend Mijatovic returns to Valencia to lead Yugoslavia's attack against Spain in one of the most intriguing of Europe's World Cup qualifying ties.
In his last outing for Yugoslavia, he hit the winner against the Czech Republic. This time, he expects it to be a lot tougher against defenders who know his style well.
